title: Template: Overload Event Communication (Load Shedding Active)
author: Nora Ahmed
body:
## Purpose
This page provides a customer-safe communication template for incidents where **Hosted API overload protection is actively shedding load** (edge admission control, routing circuit breakers, and/or runtime shed points). The goal is to:
- Set correct expectations and reduce confusion (clear 429/503 semantics, Retry-After guidance).
- Avoid ambiguous 5xx/timeouts by explicitly describing overload protection behavior.
- Ensure every update includes the minimum required facts customers need to take action.

This template is designed for:
- **Status page posts** (public)
- **Enterprise customer updates** (email / support portal)
- **In-product / console banners** (if enabled)

---

## When to use (trigger)
Use this template when any of the following are true for Hosted API:
- Load shedding is enabled and materially impacting customers (sustained elevated 429/503 due to overload).
- Circuit breakers are open/half-open for one or more (model, region, tier) combinations.
- We are returning a stable overload response intentionally (429/503) to prevent cascading failures.

Do NOT use this template for:
- Single-tenant quota enforcement (normal 429 rate limit/quota).
- A model-specific outage unrelated to overload (use model outage template).
- Dedicated-only capacity events (use Dedicated comms template; see Dedicated alignment notes below).

---

## Customer-facing language (approved terminology)
Preferred terms:
- “elevated traffic / request volume”
- “overload protection”
- “load shedding” (OK; explain once in plain language)
- “some requests may receive a 429 or 503 response with Retry-After”
- “we’re temporarily limiting request acceptance to protect overall service stability”

Avoid terms:
- “dropped traffic” / “we are dropping your requests”
- “GPU outage” (unless it is actually a GPU provider outage)
- “capacity exhausted” / “we ran out of GPUs”
- “scheduler is broken” / “KV-cache thrash” / other internal mechanisms

---

## Required fields to include in every status update
Include these even if the numbers are estimates; if unknown, say “we are assessing” and commit to next update.

1) **What is impacted**
- Product: Hosted API (and whether OpenAI-compatible endpoints are included)
- Endpoint class: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank (as applicable)
- Request type: streaming vs non-streaming (if materially different)

2) **Where**
- Regions impacted (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- Models impacted (list public model names; keep it short)

3) **What customers will see**
- HTTP status codes: 429 and/or 503 (only list what is occurring)
- Retry guidance: Retry-After header present (yes/no) and recommended client behavior

4) **Timing**
- Start time (UTC)
- Current status: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved
- Next update time (explicit)

5) **Magnitude (pick 1–2 metrics)**
Choose customer-safe, stable metrics:
- Approx. affected request rate: e.g., “a portion of requests” or “elevated 429/503 rates”
- If confident: “peak shed rate ~X% in <region>” (avoid precise numbers if they are changing rapidly)

6) **What we are doing**
Customer-safe mitigations:
- “shifting traffic” (region or capacity tier)
- “adding capacity” / “scaling up”
- “tightening overload protection thresholds temporarily” (only if Product/SRE approves wording)

---

## Update cadence (default)
- Initial post: within **10 minutes** of confirmation.
- Updates: every **30 minutes** while impact is ongoing (or sooner if meaningfully changed).
- Monitoring update: once impact is no longer observed but we are watching stability.
- Resolved: when error rates have normalized and shedding is no longer active.
- Follow-up summary: within **2 business days** (short, customer-safe).

---

## What NOT to say (hard rules)
Do not include:
- Customer names, account IDs, or identifiable traffic patterns.
- Internal hostnames, dashboards, incident channels, ticket links.
- Unverified root cause or guesses (“likely a bug”, “probably the provider”).
- Commitments to a precise ETA unless validated by Incident Commander (IC).
- Instructions that could cause retry storms (e.g., “just retry immediately”).

Do not recommend:
- Aggressive retries
- Removing backoff
- Increasing concurrency without limits

---

## Status page templates (public)
Use the most specific template that is true.

### A) Initial post (Investigating)
Title:
- “Hosted API: Elevated error rates due to overload protection in <REGION(S)>”

Body:
- “We are investigating elevated error rates for the Redwood Hosted API in <REGION(S)> starting at <START_TIME_UTC>. During this period, overload protection may cause some requests to be rejected with **HTTP 429** or **HTTP 503** responses. Clients should follow the **Retry-After** header when present and use exponential backoff with jitter. Next update by <NEXT_UPDATE_TIME_UTC>.”

Optional add-on (if model-scoped):
- “Impact is currently concentrated on <MODEL(S)>.”

### B) Identified (load shedding confirmed)
Body:
- “We have identified elevated traffic leading to saturation in <REGION(S)>. To protect overall service stability, overload protection is actively limiting request acceptance. Some requests may receive **429/503** with **Retry-After**. We are mitigating by <MITIGATION_1> and <MITIGATION_2>. Next update by <NEXT_UPDATE_TIME_UTC>.”

### C) Monitoring (shedding tapering)
Body:
- “Mitigations have reduced error rates and we are seeing recovery in <REGION(S)>. Overload protection may still trigger intermittently while we monitor stability. We will provide another update by <NEXT_UPDATE_TIME_UTC>.”

### D) Resolved
Body:
- “This issue has been resolved. Overload protection is no longer actively limiting requests in <REGION(S)>, and error rates have returned to normal levels as of <RESOLVED_TIME_UTC>. If you continue to see 429/503 errors, please contact support with request IDs and timestamps.”

### E) Follow-up summary (optional, customer-safe)
Body:
- “Summary: On <DATE>, elevated traffic in <REGION(S)> triggered overload protection which rejected a portion of requests with 429/503 to prevent broader service degradation. We mitigated by <HIGH_LEVEL_ACTIONS>. We are implementing additional safeguards and capacity improvements to reduce recurrence.”

---

## Enterprise customer update template (email / support portal)
Subject:
- “Update: Hosted API overload protection active in <REGION(S)> (429/503 with Retry-After)”

Body:
- “We are currently seeing elevated traffic impacting the Redwood Hosted API in <REGION(S)> starting at <START_TIME_UTC>. To maintain platform stability, overload protection is actively limiting request acceptance for some traffic. You may observe:
  - HTTP **429** or **503** responses
  - A **Retry-After** header on overload responses (when present)

Recommended client behavior:
- Respect **Retry-After** if provided.
- Use **exponential backoff with jitter**.
- Avoid immediate retry loops and avoid increasing concurrency during the event.

Scope (current best view):
- Regions: <REGION(S)>
- Models/endpoints: <MODEL(S)> / <ENDPOINTS>

Mitigation in progress:
- <MITIGATION_1>
- <MITIGATION_2>

Billing note:
- Requests rejected before generation begins (e.g., admission control) do not produce tokens and are not charged. If you believe you were billed for rejected requests, share timestamps and request IDs and we will investigate.

Next update:
- We will provide another update by <NEXT_UPDATE_TIME_UTC> (or sooner if conditions change).”

---

## Dedicated vs Hosted note (avoid confusion)
If asked or if customers are mixed Hosted + Dedicated:
- Approved phrasing: “Dedicated capacity is isolated and may not be affected by Hosted load shedding. If you have Dedicated endpoints and are seeing elevated latency or errors, share the endpoint name/region and we will evaluate Dedicated capacity separately.”
- Avoid: “Dedicated is never affected” (not always true if shared control plane components are degraded).

---

## Required internal metrics to capture for comms (do not paste raw dashboards publicly)
Before posting, capture the following in the internal incident doc (not the status page):
- Time window (UTC) and impacted regions
- Affected endpoints/models
- Peak and current: 429 rate, 503 rate (Hosted API)
- Shed/admission metrics (edge and runtime): shed rate %, admission rate
- Breaker states: closed/open/half-open counts by region/model class
- Queue depth / saturation signals (high level)
- p95/p99 latency trend (to confirm stabilization)
- Retry-After values currently being emitted (range)

If metrics are uncertain, say so internally and avoid publishing numbers.

---

## Internal approval + coordination checklist
1) Confirm with IC/SRE on:
- Regions/models impacted
- Whether we are actively shedding (yes/no)
- Approved customer language for the current event

2) Coordinate with Support (Customer Success):
- Ensure macros reference the same error codes and retry guidance
- Provide a single “what to tell customers” paragraph (paste from this template)

3) Verify customer guidance does not amplify load:
- No instructions that encourage rapid retries
- Retry-After is present where expected

4) Post and set next update timer.

---

## Quick reference: placeholders
Use these placeholders consistently:
- <REGION(S)>: e.g., us-east, eu-west
- <MODEL(S)>: public model names (keep to top 1–3)
- <ENDPOINTS>: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
- <START_TIME_UTC> / <NEXT_UPDATE_TIME_UTC> / <RESOLVED_TIME_UTC>
- <MITIGATION_1>/<MITIGATION_2>: “shifting traffic”, “adding capacity”, “adjusting routing policies”, “tuning overload protection thresholds” (only if approved)

---

## FAQ snippets (approved short answers)
**Q: Why am I seeing 429/503?**
A: “During traffic spikes, Redwood enables overload protection to keep the service stable. Some requests may be rejected with 429/503 and a Retry-After header so clients can retry safely.”

**Q: Should we retry?**
A: “Yes—follow Retry-After when present and use exponential backoff with jitter. Avoid immediate retry loops.”

**Q: Does this count as an outage?**
A: “We treat this as a service-impacting event. The purpose of overload protection is to prevent broader degradation while we mitigate.”

**Q: Are we billed for rejected requests?**
A: “Requests rejected before generation do not generate tokens and are not charged. If you have a billing concern, share request IDs and timestamps with support.”
